The difference in the Neighbors effect between 2004 voters and non-voters is **0.027** (0.027229, rounded to the nearest thousandth).

I compared Neighbors against Control within each 2004 turnout group, using the 2006 turnout means:

| 2004 primary voter | Control | Neighbors | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | 0.3858 | 0.4823 | 0.0965 |
| No | 0.2371 | 0.3064 | 0.0693 |

The effect for 2004 voters is 0.0965 and for non-voters is 0.0693, so the difference is 0.0965 − 0.0693 ≈ 0.027. Because treatment was randomly assigned, these simple difference-in-means estimates are valid causal effects within each subgroup. I did not fit a regression, so there are no standard errors here.

ANSWER: 0.027
